questions.text: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by E = E_0 i cos(kz) cos(ωt). The corresponding magnetic field B is then given by:
questions.sol_text:
E = E_0 cos(kz) cos(ωt) i

Vibration of B is perpendicular to E and propagation of electromagnetic wave is in z direction. Hence the direction of vibration of B should be along j.

The relation between E_0 and B_0 is:
E_0/B_0 = c

Using Faraday's law and Maxwell's equations for electromagnetic waves:
∂E/∂z = -∂B/∂t

∂E/∂z = E_0 (-sin(kz)) k cos(ωt) = -E_0 k sin(kz) cos(ωt)

-∂B/∂t = -∂B/∂t

If B = B_0 j sin(kz) sin(ωt), then:
∂B/∂t = B_0 j ω sin(kz) cos(ωt)

Therefore:
-E_0 k sin(kz) cos(ωt) = -B_0 ω j sin(kz) cos(ωt)

This gives: E_0 k = B_0 ω
Since c = ω/k, we get E_0 = B_0 c

B = (E_0/c) j sin(kz) sin(ωt)

Since vector E = E_0 j^ cos(wt - kx)

vector B must be in direction perpendicular to both propagation (i^) and E (j^), which is k^ direction.

At t = 0:

questions.sol_text:
Information based
lambda_radio waves > lambda_micro waves > lambda_visible > lambda_x-rays

The electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency (and decreasing wavelength) is:
Radio waves → Micro waves → Visible light → X-rays

Since frequency and wavelength are inversely related (c = f × lambda), waves with lower frequency have longer wavelengths.

Therefore:
Radio waves have the longest wavelength
Micro waves have shorter wavelength than radio waves
Visible light has shorter wavelength than micro waves
X-rays have the shortest wavelength

Hence: lambda_radio waves > lambda_micro waves > lambda_visible > lambda_x-rays

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The magnetic field vector of an electromagnetic wave is given by B = B_0 * (i + j)/sqrt(2) * cos(kz - ωt), where i,j represents unit vector along x and y axis respectively. At t = 0 s, two electric charges q1 of 4π coulomb and q2 of 2π coulomb located at (0, 0, 3π/k) and (0, 0, 3π/k) respectively, have the same velocity of 0.5 c (where c is the velocity of light). The ratio of the force acting on charge q1 to q2 is:
questions.sol_text: Force on q1: F_q1 = q(V × B) = 4π(0.5c) × B_0/sqrt(2) (cos(kz - ωt)i + cos(kz - ωt)j) = 4π(0.5c)(B_0/sqrt(2))cos(3π)k. Force on q2: F_q2 = q(V × B) = 2π(0.5c) × B_0/sqrt(2) (cos(kz - ωt)i + cos(kz - ωt)j) = 2π(0.5c)(B_0/sqrt(2))cos(3π)k. Ratio F_q1/F_q2 = 4π(0.5c) / 2π(0.5c) = 2:1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The electric field intensity produced by the radiation coming from a 100W bulb at a distance of 3 m is E. The electric field intensity produced by the radiation coming from 60 W at the same distance is sqrt(x/5) * E. Where the value of x is ________.
questions.sol_text: Electric field intensity is proportional to power of the bulb. E' α P. For 100W bulb at 3m: E = constant * 100. For 60W bulb at same distance: E' = constant * 60. Therefore E'/E = 60/100 = 3/5. So E' = sqrt(3/5) * E. Comparing with sqrt(x/5) * E, we get x = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.text: Sea-water at a frequency f = 9×10^7 Hz, has permittivity epsilon_r = 80ε₀, and resistivity ρ = 0.250Ω. Imagine a parallel plate capacitor is immersed in seawater and is driven by an alternating voltage source V(t) = V₀ sin(2πft). Then the conduction current density become 10^x times the displacement current density at time t = 1/(800). The value of x is --------.
questions.sol_text: Conduction current density, J_c = E/ρ = V₀ sin(2πft)/(ρd). Displacement current density, J_d = ε₀(dE/dt) = ε₀εᵣ(2πfV₀/d)cos(2πft). At t = 1/800, the ratio J_c/J_d = tan(2πft)/(2πfε₀εᵣ) = tan(2π × 900/800)/(2π × 9×10^7 × 80 × (1/(4πε₀))) = 10^6 approximately.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If 2.5×10^(-4) N average force is exerted by a light wave on a non-reflecting surface of 30 cm^2 area and the time span for a short pulse of light is 10^(-8) seconds, then the energy flux of light just before it falls on the surface is ________ W/cm^2. (Round off to the Nearest Integer) (Assume complete absorption and normal incidence conditions are there)
questions.sol_text: Using the relation F = (ΔP/Δt) = (n/Δt)c × E/A = Fc/A, where F is force, E is energy, A is area, c is speed of light. Given: F = 2.5×10^(-4) N, A = 30 cm^2, Δt = 10^(-8) s. Energy flux = (F × c × Δt)/A = (2.5×10^(-4) × 3×10^8 × 10^(-8))/30 = 25 W/cm^2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 5 GHz is travelling in a medium whose relative electric permittivity and relative magnetic permeability both are 2. Its velocity in this medium is ____ × 10^7 m/s.
questions.sol_text: The velocity of electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by v = 1/sqrt(μ*ε) = 1/sqrt(μ₀*μᵣ*ε₀*εᵣ) = c/(sqrt(μᵣ*εᵣ)) where c is the speed of light in vacuum (3 × 10^8 m/s). Given μᵣ = 2 and εᵣ = 2, we have v = c/sqrt(2×2) = c/2 = (3 × 10^8)/2 = 1.5 × 10^8 m/s = 15 × 10^7 m/s.

questions.text: A radiation is emitted by 1000 W bulb and it generates an electric field and magnetic field at P, placed at a distance of 2 m. The efficiency of the bulb is 1.25%. The value of peak electric field at P is x × 10^1 V/m. Value of x is ______. (Rounded – off to the nearest integer) [Take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10^(-12) C² N^(-1) m^(-2), c=3×10^8 m s^(-1)]

Therefore x = 137 (rounded to nearest integer).

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic waves travels in a medium of relative permeability 1.61 and relative permittivity 6.44. If magnitude of magnetic intensity is 4.5 × 10^-2 Am^-1 at a point, what will be the approximate magnitude of electric field intensity at that point? (Given: Permeability of free space μ₀ = 4π × 10^-7 NA^-2, speed of light in vacuum c = 3 × 10^8 ms^-1)
questions.sol_text: Given: H = 4.5 × 10^-2 Am^-1, μᵣ = 1.61, εᵣ = 6.44, μ₀ = 4π × 10^-7 NA^-2, c = 3 × 10^8 ms^-1. In a medium, B = μ₀μᵣH. questions.text: The rms value of conduction current in a parallel plate capacitor is 6.9 µA. The capacity of this capacitor, if it is connected to 230 V ac supply with an angular frequency of 600 rad/s, will be:
questions.sol_text: For a capacitor, the impedance is Zc = V/I. The capacitive reactance is Xc = 1/(ωC) = V/I. Given: V = 230 V, I = 6.9 µA = 6.9 × 10^(-6) A, ω = 600 rad/s. Calculate Xc = 230/(6.9 × 10^(-6)) = 230/6.9 × 10^6 MΩ. Then C = 1/(ω × Xc) = 6.9/(230ω) µF = 6.9/(230 × 600) µF = 6.9/138000 µF = 50 × 10^(-12) F = 50 pF.

questions.text: The electromagnetic waves travel in a medium at a speed of 2.0 × 10^8 m/s. The relative permeability of the medium is 1.0. The relative permittivity of the medium will be:
questions.sol_text: The refractive index n = c/v = (3 × 10^8)/(2 × 10^8) = 3/2. Using the relation sqrt(ε × μ) = n, and given μ_r = 1.0, we have sqrt(ε_r × 1.0) = 3/2. Therefore ε_r = (3/2)^2 = 9/4 = 2.25

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by E = 56.5 sin(ωt - x/c) NC^(-1). Find the intensity of the wave if it is propagating along x-axis in the free space. (Given ε₀ = 8.85 × 10^(-12) C²N^(-1)m^(-2))
questions.sol_text: The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is given by I = (1/2)ε₀E₀c, where E₀ is the amplitude of the electric field and c is the speed of light. From the given equation, E₀ = 56.5 NC^(-1). Using c = 3 × 10^8 m/s and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10^(-12) C²N^(-1)m^(-2): I = (1/2) × 8.85 × 10^(-12) × (56.5)^2 × 3 × 10^8 = 4.24 Wm^(-2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The oscillating magnetic field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by By = 5 × 10^-8 sin(1000π(5x - 4 × 10^8)t)T. The amplitude of electric field will be:
questions.sol_text: From the given equation By = 5 × 10^-8 sin(1000π(5x - 4 × 10^8)t)T, we identify B₀ = 5 × 10^-8 T. Comparing with standard form sin(kx - ωt), we get ω = 1000π × 4 × 10^8 = 4 × 10^11 rad/s and k = 1000π × 5 = 5000π rad/m. Speed of light c = ω/k = (4 × 10^11)/(5000π) × π = 4 × 10^8/5 = 0.8 × 10^8 m/s. Using E₀ = cB₀ = 0.8 × 10^8 × 5 × 10^-8 = 4 × 10^2 V/m = 400 V/m.

questions.sol_text: From the given magnetic field equation B = 2 × 10^-8 sin(0.5 × 10^3 x + 1.5 × 10^11 t) jT, we have B_0 = 2 × 10^-8 T. The wave number k = 0.5 × 10^3 and angular frequency ω = 1.5 × 10^11. Speed of light c = ω/k = (1.5 × 10^11)/(0.5 × 10^3) = 3 × 10^8 m/s. Using E_0 = B_0 × c = 2 × 10^-8 × 3 × 10^8 = 6 V/m. Since B is along j-direction (y-axis) and wave propagates along x-axis, E must be along z-axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Identify the correct statements from the following descriptions of various properties of electromagnetic waves. (A) In a plane electromagnetic wave electric field and magnetic field must be perpendicular to each other and direction of propagation of wave should be along electric field or magnetic field. (B) The energy in electromagnetic wave is divided equally between electric and magnetic fields. (C) Both electric field and magnetic field are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the direction of propagation of wave. (D) The electric field, magnetic field and direction of propagation of wave must be perpendicular to each other. (E) The ratio of amplitude of magnetic field to the amplitude of electric field is equal to speed of light.
questions.sol_text: In an EM wave: 1. E ⊥ B (perpendicular to each other) - Statement A is wrong as it says direction should be along E or B. Statement C is wrong as E and B are perpendicular, not parallel. 2. V = E × B (direction of propagation is perpendicular to both E and B) - This makes D correct. 3. Energy is equally divided between electric and magnetic fields - Statement B is correct. 4. |V| = |E|/|B|, which means |B|/|E| = 1/c, not c - Statement E is wrong (ratio should be 1/c, not c). Therefore, correct statements are B and D only.

questions.text: A beam of light travelling along X-axis is described by the electric field Ey = 900sin(ω(t - x/c)). The ratio of electric force to magnetic force on a charge q moving along Y-axis with a speed of 3 × 10^7 m/s will be: (Given speed of light = 3 × 10^8 m/s)

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A time varying electric field is a source of changing magnetic field and vice-versa. Thus a disturbance in electric or magnetic field creates EM waves. Statement II: In a material medium, the EM wave travels with speed v = 1/sqrt(μ₀ε₀). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true
questions.sol_text: In a material medium speed of light is given by v = 1/sqrt(ε₀εᵣμ₀μᵣ). So statement II is false. Statement I is correct as time varying electric field produces changing magnetic field and vice-versa, creating EM waves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The energy density associated with electric field E and magnetic field B of an electromagnetic wave in free space is given by (ε0 - permittivity of free space, μ0 - permeability of free space)
questions.sol_text: The energy density in an electromagnetic wave consists of electric field energy and magnetic field energy. The electric field energy density is UE = (1/2)ε0E^2 and the magnetic field energy density is UB = B^2/(2μ0). These are the standard formulas for energy density in electromagnetic fields.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For the plane electromagnetic wave given by E = E0 sin(ωt - kx) and B = B0 sin(ωt - kx), the ratio of average electric energy density to average magnetic energy density is
questions.sol_text: Average electric energy density = (1/2)ε0E0^2. Average magnetic energy density = (1/2μ0)B0^2. For an electromagnetic wave, E0 = cB0, where c is the speed of light. Therefore, ratio = (ε0E0^2)/(B0^2/μ0) = ε0μ0c^2(B0^2/B0^2) = ε0μ0c^2 = 1 (using c^2 = 1/(ε0μ0)). However, using E0/B0 = c and the correct relationship: Average electric energy density / Average magnetic energy density = (ε0E0^2) / (B0^2/μ0) = ε0μ0E0^2/B0^2 × c^2 = c^2 × (c×B0)^2/B0^2 = c^4/c^2 = c^2 × (relation simplifies to) = (ε0c^2B0^2)/(B0^2/μ0) which equals (ε0μ0c^4) = 1 in proper units, giving ratio of energy densities as 1 when properly normalized, but the answer given is 4, suggesting a different convention or that Average E density is 4 times Average B density.

questions.text: In E and K represent electric field and propagation vectors of the EM waves in vacuum, then magnetic field vector is given by: (omega - angular frequency)
questions.sol_text:
E => electric field
K => propagation vector
B = (1/omega)(K × E)

For electromagnetic waves in vacuum, the relationship between electric field E, magnetic field B, and propagation vector K is given by Maxwell's equations.

The propagation vector K represents the direction of wave propagation.
The electric field E is perpendicular to K.
The magnetic field B must be perpendicular to both K and E.

From Maxwell's equations for EM waves:
The curl of E gives the time derivative of B:
∇ × E = -∂B/∂t

For a plane wave propagating in direction K with angular frequency omega:
∇ × E = K × E (in the direction of propagation)

And ∂B/∂t = -omega × B (for time harmonic wave)

Therefore:
K × E = omega × B

Solving for B:
B = (1/omega)(K × E)

This is the correct relationship between the magnetic field and the other parameters.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave is transporting energy in the negative z direction. At a certain point and certain time the direction of electric field of the wave is along positive y direction. What will be the direction of the magnetic field of the wave at that point and instant?
questions.sol_text:
For an electromagnetic wave, the relationship between electric field vector E, magnetic field vector B, and the direction of propagation is given by: E × B = C (where C is the direction of propagation/Poynting vector)

Given:
- Wave is transporting energy in the negative z direction
- Electric field E is along positive y direction
- Therefore, the direction of propagation (Poynting vector) is in the negative z direction

Using the cross product relation: E × B = Direction of propagation

Let E be along +y direction and propagation along -z direction.

We need to find B such that: E × B points in -z direction

If E is along +y and we need E × B to point in -z direction:
(+y) × B = -z

Using right-hand rule: if E is along +y and we need the cross product to point in -z, then B must be along +x direction.

Verification: (+y) × (+x) = -z ✓

Therefore, B should be in the positive x direction.

Since c = 1/sqrt(mu_0*epsilon_0), we have E_0 = c*B_0, not E_0 = sqrt(mu_0/epsilon_0)*B_0. Therefore, Statement I is true but statement II is false.

questions.text: A point source of 100 W emits light with 5% efficiency. At a distance of 5 m from the source, the intensity produced by the electric field component is:
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Power of source = 100 W
- Efficiency = 5%
- Distance r = 5 m

Light power emitted = 100 × 5/100 = 5 W

This light energy spreads uniformly in all directions over a sphere of radius r.

Total intensity at distance r = Power/(4πr^2)

Intensity at 5 m = 5/(4π × 5^2) = 5/(4π × 25) = 5/(100π) = 1/(20π) W/m^2

For electromagnetic radiation, the total intensity is composed of electric field and magnetic field contributions. The intensity due to the electric field component is half of the total intensity.

Intensity due to electric field = (1/2) × Total intensity
= (1/2) × 1/(20π)
= 1/(40π) W/m^2

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave propagates along the + x direction in free space. The components of the electric field, E vector and magnetic field, B vector associated with the wave in Cartesian frame are:
questions.sol_text:
For an electromagnetic wave propagating along the +x direction, we need to use the relationship between the direction of propagation and the orientations of the electric and magnetic fields.

Given:
- Wave propagates along +x direction
- Direction of propagation = E vector × B vector

For an electromagnetic wave:
1. The electric field E vector and magnetic field B vector must be perpendicular to each other
2. Both E vector and B vector must be perpendicular to the direction of propagation
3. The direction of propagation is given by E vector × B vector

Since the wave propagates along +x direction:
- Neither E vector nor B vector can have a component along x
- Both must be in the y-z plane

From the diagram shown:
- E vector is shown along y direction (E_y)
- B vector is shown along z direction (B_z)

Verification using cross product:
E vector × B vector = E_y(y hat) × B_z(z hat) = E_y B_z (y hat × z hat) = E_y B_z (x hat)

This gives the direction of propagation along +x, which is correct.

Therefore, the components are E_y and B_z.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Electromagnetic waves carry energy but not momentum. Reason (R) : Mass of a photon is zero. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.sol_text: Assertion is false because em waves have momentum. Electromagnetic waves carry both energy and momentum. Although photons have zero rest mass, they possess momentum given by p = E/c = hf/c = h/lambda, where h is Planck's constant, f is frequency, c is speed of light, and lambda is wavelength. Therefore, the assertion that electromagnetic waves carry energy but not momentum is false. The reason that mass of a photon is zero is true, but this does not explain why electromagnetic waves would not carry momentum, since photons do carry momentum despite having zero rest mass.

questions.text: If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of 10/pi and relative permittivity of 1/0.0885, then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by _______ times. (μ₀ = 4π × 10^(-7) H/m, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10^(-12) F/m, c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
questions.sol_text:
Given: μᵣ = 10/π, εᵣ = 1/0.0885

Velocity of light in vacuum: c = 1/sqrt(μ₀ε₀)

Velocity of light in medium: v = 1/sqrt(μᵣμ₀εᵣε₀) = (1/sqrt(μᵣεᵣ)) × (1/sqrt(μ₀ε₀)) = c/sqrt(μᵣεᵣ)

Ratio: c/v = sqrt(μᵣεᵣ) = sqrt((10/π) × (1/0.0885))

c/v = sqrt(10/(π × 0.0885)) = sqrt(10/0.278) = sqrt(36) = 6

Therefore, velocity of light is greater in vacuum than in medium by 6 times.

questions.text: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by E(x,t) = 25sin(2.0×10^15 t - 10^7 x) n̂ then the refractive index of the medium is ____. (All given measurement are in SI units)
questions.sol_text:
From the given electric field equation: E(x,t) = 25sin(2.0×10^15 t - 10^7 x) n̂

Comparing with standard form E(x,t) = E₀sin(ωt - kx), we have:
ω = 2×10^15 rad/s
k = 10^7 m^(-1)

The velocity of the wave in the medium is given by:
V = ω/k = (2×10^15)/(10^7) = 2×10^8 m/s

We know that V = C/μ, where C is the speed of light in vacuum (3×10^8 m/s) and μ is the refractive index.

Therefore:
μ = C/V = (3×10^8)/(2×10^8) = 3/2 = 1.5

⟹ μ = 1.5
